title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 120: The Viking Longship: Maritime Masters of the North
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 120 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Viking Longship: Maritime Masters of the North

Paragraph 1. Between the years 750 and 1100 CE, Scandinavian sailors called the Vikings travelled far across Europe and North America. Their secret was an amazing wooden boat: the Viking longship. It was fast and strong enough to cross wide oceans, yet small enough to travel up shallow rivers.

Paragraph 2. Viking builders made their ships in a very smart way. First, they shaped a long, strong piece of oak wood for the bottom of the boat. Next, they put thin wooden boards on the outside so each board overlapped the next one. They joined the boards with iron nails and stuffed tarred animal wool between the boards to stop water from coming in. Finally, they tied the inside wooden frame using bendy tree roots instead of hard metal nails. Because of this, the ship bent smoothly with big ocean waves instead of breaking.

Paragraph 3. The longship had two pointed ends that looked the same. Sailors could quickly change direction without turning the boat around. Also, the ship needed less than one metre of water to float. Because of this, Vikings could sail close to land and land straight onto sandy beaches without needing deep ports. In calm water, crews used long wooden oars, and in open seas they raised a big wool sail covered with sheep fat.

Paragraph 4. In 1904, scientists in Norway found a famous 9th-century Viking boat called the Oseberg ship. It stayed in great condition because it was buried inside wet blue clay. Later discoveries in Denmark proved that Vikings built different boats for different jobs: narrow ships for war and wide ships for carrying goods.

q5.text: Viking longships could travel on both deep oceans and shallow rivers.

steps: Đoạn 1: Đủ khỏe để vượt đại dương và đủ nhỏ để đi ngược sông nông.

q6.text: Builders used hard metal nails to attach the inside wooden frame.

steps: Đoạn 2: Khung bên trong được buộc bằng rễ cây mềm dẻo (bendy tree roots), không đóng đinh cứng.

q7.text: Viking ships needed a large deep-water port to turn around.

steps: Đoạn 3: Hai đầu giống nhau giúp đổi hướng nhanh mà không cần quay đầu tàu hay cần cảng sâu.

q8.text: Viking sailors used glass telescopes to watch coastlines from far away.

steps: Đoạn 3: Bài không đề cập đến kính viễn vọng.
